meta.title: About us
meta.description: EtnoJourney designs small cultural journeys led by village hosts, with a fair share for communities and respect for tradition.

about.title: Journeys led by the people who host them
about.description: We believe the best way to understand a culture is through the people who live it every day, not through a stage set up for tourists.

mission.title: Opening doors, not putting traditions on display
body: EtnoJourney connects travellers with customary and village communities across Indonesia. Every journey is designed together with local hosts: they decide what can be shared, when, and how.
We deliberately keep journeys small and slow. The goal is not to collect as many places as possible, but to make time to sit, listen and learn from your hosts.

paths.title: Three ways to travel with Etno Journey
paths.intro: Etno Journey follows three paths: ancestral traditions, inner journeys and the living earth. Each is a way of travelling slowly, alongside the people who keep these places alive.
paths.note: Not every experience below is a bookable tour yet. These are experiences we develop with our partner communities; where a tour already exists, we link to it.

traditions.title: Discover ancestral traditions that shape identity and wisdom
traditions.intro: Step into living heritage, where rituals, crafts and stories illuminate the timeless wisdom of the ancestors.

items.title: Sacred rituals and ceremonies
items.body: Seasonal offerings, temple rites and harvest celebrations, joined with respect.

items.title: Heritage crafts and artistry
items.body: Weaving, woodcarving, pottery and batik, learned at the artisan's side.

items.title: Storytelling and oral heritage
items.body: Myths, genealogies and memories, told by the elders who carry them.

items.title: Traditional healing practices
items.body: Herbal medicine and ancestral therapies, as their keepers choose to share them.

items.title: Music, dance and performance
items.body: Gamelan, chants and sacred dances in the setting they belong to.

items.title: Culinary journeys
items.body: Ancestral recipes cooked and shared with local families.

items.title: Pilgrimage to sacred landscapes
items.body: Ancestral paths to temples, shrines and natural landmarks.

items.title: Dialogue with custodians of tradition
items.body: Conversations with priests, healers, artisans and cultural leaders.

traditions.closing: Etno Journey turns heritage into experience, inviting you to live traditions, embrace wisdom and carry identity forward.

inner.title: Embark on inner journeys that nurture mindfulness and meaning
inner.intro: Experiences designed to quiet the mind, awaken awareness and cultivate a deeper sense of purpose.

items.title: Guided meditation retreats
items.body: Unhurried days of guided practice in quiet places.

items.title: Breathwork and pranayama
items.body: Breathing practices that steady the body and the mind.

items.title: Silent nature walks
items.body: Walking without words, listening to the land.

items.title: Mindful journaling circles
items.body: Writing and sharing reflections from the road.

items.title: Yoga for inner awareness
items.body: Gentle movement that turns attention inward.

items.title: Sacred sound immersion
items.body: Resting in the sound of bells, gongs and chants.

items.title: Contemplative dialogue with elders
items.body: Slow conversations about life, meaning and belonging.

items.title: Mindful culinary rituals
items.body: Preparing and eating food with full attention and gratitude.

inner.closing: Etno Journey invites you to embrace mindfulness as a living practice, weaving silence, sound, movement and reflection into journeys that nurture meaning and inner harmony.

nature.title: Embrace nature in its pure essence
nature.intro: Celebrate the living earth through experiences that honour balance, beauty and the sacred harmony of <term>Mamahayu Hayuning Bawana</term>: the balance of life and the beauty of the world.

items.title: Ecological immersion walks
items.body: Through rice terraces, forests and along rivers.

items.title: Water blessing rituals
items.body: Purification at sacred springs and rivers, guided by the community.

items.title: Tree planting and conservation
items.body: Hands-on work with local conservation efforts.

items.title: Wildlife and biodiversity encounters
items.body: Meeting the life of a place without disturbing it.

items.title: Organic farming experience
items.body: Working the fields with farmers who grow without chemicals.

items.title: Sunset and firelight gatherings
items.body: Evenings of stories and stillness as the day ends.

items.title: Dialogue on sustainability
items.body: Learning how communities care for their land and water.

nature.closing: Etno Journey makes nature a sacred companion, inviting you to walk gently, live mindfully and honour the balance of life and the beauty of the world.

principles.title: Four principles we don't compromise on

fair.title: A fair share
fair.body: Guides and host families are paid directly for their time and expertise, and part of every booking goes to village needs that the community decides for itself.

small.title: Small groups
small.body: Every tour has a participant limit. Small groups mean more honest conversations and a lighter footprint on the village.

consent.title: Consent for every ceremony
consent.body: Ceremonies belong to the community. Guests only attend when hosts allow it, and we follow their rules on dress, photography and boundaries that must not be crossed.

real.title: No staged performances
real.body: We never hold rituals just for guests. What you meet is everyday life: kitchens, fields, workshops and ceremonies that are genuinely taking place.

responsible.title: What we ask of every guest
items: Dress modestly and follow your hosts' guidance, especially at temples, customary houses and ceremonies.
Ask before photographing people, and accept a no gracefully.
Take your rubbish home and use water sparingly, especially in villages where it is scarce.
Buy crafts directly from their makers and respect the prices they set.

partners.title: How we choose and support our partners
body: We work with villages whose residents themselves want to welcome guests. Before a journey opens, we agree with elders and village managers on group sizes, schedules that don't interfere with customary activities, and how income is shared.
Partnerships are reviewed regularly. If a village needs a pause, for example during a major ceremony season or the harvest, we put journeys on hold.

cta.title: Ready to be a good guest?
cta.body: See the journeys that are open now and choose the one that suits your pace.

meta.title: FAQ
meta.description: Answers about booking, payment, preparing for your trip, cultural etiquette and your EtnoJourney account.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: Can't find what you need? Reach us through the contact details at the bottom of the page.

items.q: How far in advance do I need to book?
items.a: Book at least 3 days before your travel date, counted in Western Indonesia Time (WIB). Hosts need that time to prepare.

Once your booking is created, select Pay now. You'll be taken to the Midtrans payment page to choose a method such as bank transfer, e-wallet or QRIS. As soon as the payment succeeds, the booking is confirmed automatically.

items.q: Is my booking guaranteed straight away?
items.a: Your seats are held from the moment you book, and the booking is confirmed as soon as payment is received. Until then its status is Pending.

Yes, as long as the booking hasn't been paid. Go to My Account, choose the booking and select Cancel. For paid bookings, cancellations and refunds are handled manually by our team under the Cancellation policy.

items.q: I've already paid but want to change the date. What should I do?
items.a: Contact us with your booking code (in the format EJ-XXXXXX). Changes depend on the hosts' availability on the new date.
The meeting point is listed on each tour page and on your booking detail page.
Every tour lists What's included, such as a local guide, meals or transport. Anything not on that list isn't included in the price.

items.q: What if I have special needs, such as food allergies?
items.a: Add them in the notes field when you book. We pass them on to your hosts before the trip.
Modest clothing that covers shoulders and knees. For temple visits in Bali, a sarong and sash are usually provided when listed under What's included.
Always ask your guide first. Some parts of a ceremony may not be photographed at all, and that must be respected.

items.q: Are ceremonies held especially for guests?
items.a: No. We never stage rituals for tourists. If a ceremony is taking place and the hosts allow it, you're invited to attend as a respectful guest.

items.q: When can I write a review?
items.a: Once the trip's status is Completed. The Write a review button appears in My Account, and each booking can be reviewed once.

items.q: Which language are EtnoJourney emails sent in?
items.a: The language you choose under My Account, Settings. Bahasa Indonesia and English are available.
Use the Forgot password link on the sign-in page. We'll email you a link to create a new password, valid for 1 hour.

meta.title: Cancellation policy
meta.description: Terms for cancellations, date changes and refunds for EtnoJourney trips.

cancellation.title: Cancellation policy
cancellation.description: How cancellations and refunds are handled, for both unpaid and paid bookings.

sections.title: Unpaid bookings
paragraphs: While a booking is Pending and unpaid, you can cancel it yourself at any time from My Account, free of charge.

sections.title: Paid bookings
paragraphs: You can cancel a paid booking yourself from My Account as long as the travel date hasn't passed. Before you confirm, you'll see which terms apply and how much will be refunded.
The refund depends on the number of days between the day you cancel and the travel date:

sections.title: Cancellation by EtnoJourney or the hosts
paragraphs: We may cancel a trip in case of safety risks, natural disasters, or if the village decides to close visits for customary activities. In that case you can choose a replacement date or a full refund.

sections.title: How refunds are processed
paragraphs: Refunds are processed manually to the original payment method through Midtrans. How long they take to arrive depends on your bank or e-wallet provider, so we can't promise an exact time. We'll email you as soon as the refund has been sent.

sections.title: Date changes
paragraphs: You can change the travel date yourself from My Account, for paid and unpaid bookings, as long as the new date is available.
For changes outside the terms below, contact us with your booking code. Requests are handled according to the hosts' availability.

meta.title: Privacy policy
meta.description: What data EtnoJourney collects, why, and how you can control it.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.description: We only keep the data needed to run your bookings and your account.

sections.title: Data controller
paragraphs: Personal data on this site is managed by [Company name], located at [Registered address].

sections.title: Data we store
paragraphs: We store the following data:
items: Account data: name, email address, a hashed password (never the plain text) and your email language.
Booking data: tour, travel date, number of travellers, contact name and phone number, the notes you write, and the price.
Payment status: status, payment method, amount and payment time as reported by Midtrans.
Reviews you write, with the name and country you provide.
Session data: IP address and user agent of the device used to sign in, for account security.

sections.title: Card and payment data
paragraphs: Payments are processed by Midtrans. Card numbers, bank details and e-wallet credentials are entered directly on the Midtrans page and are never stored on our systems.

sections.title: How we use data
paragraphs: We use data to:
items: Create and manage bookings, including passing special needs on to your hosts.
Send transactional emails: booking confirmations, status changes, payments and password resets.
Keep accounts secure, for example by limiting repeated sign-in attempts.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: We only use two kinds of cookie: a session cookie to keep you signed in, and a language cookie to remember your site language. We currently use no analytics, advertising or third-party tracking cookies.

sections.title: Third parties
paragraphs: Data is shared only with parties needed to provide the service:
items: Our email provider, to send transactional emails.
Your hosts and guides, limited to the contact name, number of travellers and relevant notes.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: You can change your name and language at any time in My Account. To request a copy or deletion of your data, contact us. Some booking data may need to be kept longer for accounting purposes: [Data retention period].

terms.title: Terms and conditions
terms.description: The basic rules that apply when you use this site and book a trip.

sections.title: The service
paragraphs: EtnoJourney, operated by [Company name], offers bookings for cultural journeys guided by local communities. By using this site, you agree to the terms below.

sections.title: Your account
paragraphs: You're responsible for keeping your password confidential and for activity on your account. The information you provide must be accurate and up to date.

sections.title: Bookings and prices
paragraphs: Prices are shown in Indonesian rupiah per person and recalculated by the system when the booking is made. Bookings must be made at least 3 days before the travel date and are subject to tour capacity. A booking is confirmed once payment is received.

sections.title: Conduct during the trip
paragraphs: Guests must follow their guide's directions and local customary rules. Hosts may end the participation of guests who break those rules or endanger others, without a refund.

sections.title: Reviews
paragraphs: Reviews can only be written for completed trips, once per booking. We may hide reviews containing hate speech, other people's personal data, or content unrelated to the trip.
